classification.difficultyReason: Combine product and chain rules, simplify over a common denominator, and check whether numerator zeros lie in the derivative's domain.

content.prompt:
Differentiate each function using the product rule.
Combine the terms using a common denominator and factor the numerator completely.
State the values of $x$ for which the derivative is zero.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}u&=6x, &u'&=6\\v&=(x+1)^{1/2}, &v'&=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+1}}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y'&=u'v+uv'\\y'&=6\sqrt{x+1}+\frac{3x}{\sqrt{x+1}}\\y'&=\frac{6(x+1)+3x}{\sqrt{x+1}}\\y'&=\frac{3(3x+2)}{\sqrt{x+1}}\end{align*}$$
For $y'=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3x+2&=0\\x&=-\frac23\end{align*}$$
This value satisfies $x>-1$, so the derivative is zero at $x=-\dfrac23$.

$$\begin{align*}u&=-4x, &u'&=-4\\v&=(1-2x)^{1/2}\\v'&=\frac12(1-2x)^{-1/2}(-2)\\v'&=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-2x}}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y'&=u'v+uv'\\y'&=-4\sqrt{1-2x}+\frac{4x}{\sqrt{1-2x}}\\y'&=\frac{-4(1-2x)+4x}{\sqrt{1-2x}}\\y'&=\frac{4(3x-1)}{\sqrt{1-2x}}\end{align*}$$
For $y'=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3x-1&=0\\x&=\frac13\end{align*}$$
This value satisfies $x<\dfrac12$, so the derivative is zero at $x=\dfrac13$.

answer.short: $y'=\dfrac{10x(5x-2)}{\sqrt{2x-1}}$. There are no values of $x$ for which the derivative is zero.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}u&=10x^2, &u'&=20x\\v&=(2x-1)^{1/2}\\v'&=\frac12(2x-1)^{-1/2}(2)\\v'&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x-1}}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}y'&=u'v+uv'\\y'&=20x\sqrt{2x-1}+\frac{10x^2}{\sqrt{2x-1}}\\y'&=\frac{20x(2x-1)+10x^2}{\sqrt{2x-1}}\\y'&=\frac{10x(5x-2)}{\sqrt{2x-1}}\end{align*}$$
The numerator is zero when
$$\begin{align*}10x(5x-2)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }\frac25\end{align*}$$
The derivative requires $x>\dfrac12$. Neither candidate is in this domain, so there are no values of $x$ for which the derivative is zero.
